newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: TWO THIRDS OF CHARLEVILLE HOUSES AFFECTED BY WATER
The Shire mayor at Charleville says two thirds of houses and properties in the south-west Queensland town have been affected by water during this week's floods.
But Graham Andrews says the exact number of homes affected and the extent of damage in them still has to be determined, though he thinks the number will be less than original thought.
Authorities will meet in Charleville this morning to begin planning a big cleanup, now that the Warrego River is slowly dropping after peaking last night.
Almost 800 people spent the night in emergency accommodation with the army and Red Cross providing meals for 14-hundred.
Meanwhile, Queensland's Natural Resources Minister, Howard Hobbs, says the town may have to think again about building levees, having rejected them after the 1990 floods.
NEW FLIGHT PATHS FOR SYDNEY AIRPORT
Some people living east and west of Sydney Airport will experience more aircraft noise under proposed new flight paths announced by the Federal Government.
There'll also be more flights over Botany Bay, to the airport's south.
But there'll be relief for residents to the airport's north, under the plan, designed to share the burden of aircraft noise more equitably.
Aircraft movements over suburbs to the north of the airport will be cut from the 1995 peak of 50 per-cent to 17 per-cent.
Federal Transport minister John Sharp says if the proposed flight paths are established, they'll operate for the long-term.
WOMAN DENIES SENATOR'S ALLEGATIONS
A woman who has applied for an apprehended violence order against Liberal Senator Bob Woods, has denied his allegations that she has been harassing him and his family.
The woman's denial comes as Liberal Senators close ranks behind Senator Woods, who's announced his resignation from Parliament.
He has been granted leave of absence from the Senate for the rest of the week.
Tasmanian Liberal Senator, Paul Calvert, says he's surprised by the allegations levelled against Senator Woods, but there's been no proof they're true.
LIBERAL UNEASE OVER POSTAL VOTE FOR REPUBLIC CONVENTION
A Federal Liberal MP wants a compulsory ballot box vote for delegates to this year's Constitutional Convention, rather than a voluntary postal vote, proposed by the Prime Minister.
The Convention, in either November or December, will discuss whether Australia should become a Republic and other options for constitutional change.
Half the delegates will be appointed by the Federal Government with the other half elected by the public.
Liberal MP, Joe Hockey, says there've been questions over the effectiveness of postal votes for some time.
NO CUT IN OFFICIAL INTEREST RATES
The Australian Chamber of Manufactures says the Reserve Bank is continuing to be reactive rather than proactive by not announcing another cut in official interest rates.

Yesterday's first Reserve Bank Board meeting of the year co-incided with news of disappointing retail sales in the December quarter leading to predictions of zero economic growth. The Chamber's national chief executive Allan Handberg, says there's a sense of disappointment the Reserve Bank has held steady on rates.
He says his organisation sees no real benefit from the bank sitting on interest rates, and most commentators were taken aback by the retail figures.
GEELONG MAN REMANDED OVER DEATH OF ELDERLY WOMAN
A 19-year old Geelong man has been remanded in custody on charges relating to the death of a 74-year old woman last month, including murder and rape.
Mark Thomas England was also charged with arson, burglary and theft, but entered no plea, when he appeared in Melbourne Magistrates Court this morning.

Police who arrested Mr England last night say he told them he'd intended a burglary, had discovered Edna Findlay in the house and had beaten her with a jemmy bar, before assulting her. They allege he stole one thousand dollars and a watch before setting the house alight with petrol.
England is to reappear in court for statement in two weeks. - - - -
WARNING ABOUT SNAKES
The National Parks and Wildlife Service has issued a warning about snakes, after two people were bitten this week, in New South Wales.
A 56-year-old Central Coast man was given six bottles of antivenene last night, after he was biten by a deadly mainland tiger snake on his farm.
Earlier this week, a Hunter Valley woman was treated at hospital after being bitten by a red-belly black snake.
Rangers say snakes are particularly active at this time of year, and people should try to stay clear of them.
